scope.summary: Implement FBX animated-garment delivery with dense auto-key bake via the Blender-bridge conversion path (MD 2026.0 auto-key parity, R-ANIM-039): the export job emits glTF/Alembic-shim/OBJ-sequence artifacts plus a generated headless Blender script (extends the MT-323 bridge generator and MT-440 shim pattern) that bakes one joint-transform key per frame in the export range and writes the FBX from Blender. Native Rust FBX writing remains PROHIBITED per Master Spec 13.12 (no FBX writer in tailor-solver or handshake_core).
acceptance_criteria: The animation export API offers export_format='fbx_bridge' alongside glTF/Alembic-shim/OBJ-sequence; selecting it generates a headless Blender bake script plus the intermediate cache artifacts the script consumes.

The generated script bakes joint transforms at every frame in the export range (auto-key), not only at frames that have an authored keyframe in the Tailor timeline; empty frames receive explicit keys interpolated per the Tailor timeline curves before writing.

A garment animated with 3 sparse avatar-pose keyframes produces, through the bridge, an FBX with N dense joint-transform keys (one per frame); re-importing that FBX in headless Blender reconstructs the pose curve within float32 tolerance.
The export range parameters from MT-418 (frame-range export) apply to the fbx_bridge path.
No FBX-writing code is added to tailor-solver or handshake_core; the only FBX writer invoked is Blender via the generated script (Master Spec 13.12 prohibition upheld).
scope.risk_if_missed: FBX handoff to Maya, Blender, and UE with sparse keyframe sources produces drifting or snapping joint animation in the downstream DCC. MD 2026.0 auto-keys are the standard industry expectation for FBX cloth animation delivery. Implementing this as a native Rust FBX writer instead of the bridge path would violate Master Spec 13.12 and take on the unmaintainable FBX-write burden the format research rejected (no mature Rust FBX writer exists; ufbx_write is immature).

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.

minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.

Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
